name: veterinary_clinic_system_088_comms_volume_by_channel
instruction: Generate the monthly communications volume dashboard. Create one ops_reports row report='comms_volume' with the episode batch_code, total (count of all communications), by_channel (JSON channel -> count), by_direction (JSON direction -> count), by_channel_direction (nested JSON channel -> direction -> count), by_owner (JSON owner_id -> count for every owner with at least one communication, sorted by owner_id ascending), top_3_owners (array of [owner_id, count] for the three owners with the most communications, sorted descending by count then ascending by owner_id for ties), and latest_occurred_at (the latest occurred_at timestamp among all communications, as a full ISO string). Compute all values from live communications; do not hardcode counts or ids.
_max_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session
_par_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session

success_criteria.summary: One ops_reports row report='comms_volume' with batch_code, total, by_channel, by_direction, by_channel_direction, by_owner, top_3_owners, and latest_occurred_at. Every aggregate is computed two independent ways (raw-row Python vs SQL) and must agree. by_owner must include all owners with at least one communication; top_3_owners must break ties by owner_id ascending.

checks.expect: Exact ops_reports row with all nested JSON fields computed from live communications.
Total, channel counts, direction counts, channel-direction cross-tabs, owner counts, and max occurred_at are computed by independent SQL and raw-row filter and must agree.

hazards: by_channel and by_direction must be ordinary JSON objects, not nested objects or arrays; total must equal the sum of by_channel and the sum of by_direction.
by_channel_direction must be a nested JSON object with channel as the outer key and direction as the inner key; its inner sums must equal by_channel and by_direction.
by_owner must use string owner_id keys and include every owner with at least one communication; the seed has 160 communications, each owned by a different owner (ids 1-160), so by_owner has 160 keys.
top_3_owners must be an array of [owner_id, count] pairs. Because every owner has exactly one communication, the top three are [1,1], [2,1], [3,1]; tie-breaking by owner_id ascending is required.
latest_occurred_at must be the full ISO string from the data (2026-09-03T21:08:40.950+00:00 in the snapshot), not a truncated date or the episode date.

Dual-path SQL vs raw-row verification is required, and the top-3 tie-breaker and full-ISO timestamp are subtle.
